title: Provisional Escrow Tokens and Model Provenance Timeline for Restricted Weights
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: When ingesting third-party models with encumbered or unclear weights, current onboarding forces a hard quarantine or full rejection which delays engineering validation and slows model vetting cycles. We need a controlled, auditable way for internal teams (and vetted external partners later) to run limited evaluations and publish performance profiles without exposing restricted artifacts or violating license terms.

Proposal: Implement a Provisional Escrow Token (PET) workflow + a Model Provenance Timeline UI. PETs are short-lived, auditable tokens that grant ephemeral access to a secured escrow of the model artifact for internal evaluation workloads only. Access is mediated by policy (license risk score, requester role, environment) and logged with immutable provenance metadata. The Console will surface a timeline view that shows every onboarding step (upload, license scan results, escrow grant, eval runs, pin events, approvals) and links to artifacts/PRs. The flow reduces time-to-evaluate while preserving legal/compliance controls and providing a clear audit trail for later remediation.
acceptance_criteria: Console shows a Model Provenance Timeline for an onboarding request with entries for upload, SPDX/license analysis, escrow token issuance, evaluation runs, and final approval/rejection.
PET API: Create/Validate/Revoke PET endpoints exist and respect TTL, scope (internal-only), and requester role checks.
Escrow storage: artifacts are stored encrypted, access requires PET and KMS decryption; every access is logged in immutable audit logs.
Automated license gating: license scanner returns a risk score; PET issuance is blocked for high-risk encumbrances unless Legal explicitly approves.
Behavioral guardrails: models accessed via PET cannot be exported or shared; outputs from evaluations are masked when necessary and human-readable provenance is attached.
End-to-end integration tests and a security review sign-off completed before canary release.
Docs: onboarding runbook, Legal FAQ, and internal how-to created and linked from the Console.
Metrics: reduction in time from upload to first internal eval by >=40% for restricted models (measured in first 30 days post-release).
technical_considerations: PETs are bearer tokens stored hashed in DB; TTL default 72 hours but configurable per-project; revocation implemented via deny-list.
Escrow store implemented on existing S3 bucket with object-level encryption + KMS; access enforced by a mediator service that validates PET, requester role, and license-policy cache.
License scanner: use SPDX parsing + custom regex detectors for encumbered clauses; return structured risk score (low/medium/high) and flagged clauses for Legal review.
Provenance Timeline events are append-only and signed by the service identity key; UI reads an event feed (paginated) for display.
Audit logs pushed to existing observability pipeline with additional fields: pet_id_hash, actor_id, action, artifact_hash, license_flags.
Scale note: typical internal eval loads will be small inference jobs but may spawn ephemeral Dedicated capacity; add quota/guardrails to prevent accidental production runs.
Security trade-offs: PETs reduce quarantine friction but increase short-lived access surface; mitigation: strict role checks, default internal-only scopes, mandatory legal hold for high-risk cases.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal alpha) behind feature-flag in Console; available to Platform and Applied ML teams only (2 weeks).
Phase 1 (dogfood) open to internal product teams + select partner engineers with NDAs (4 weeks); monitor audit logs and license exception requests.
Phase 2 (canary) enable for a subset of customers with opt-in and legal attestation workflow (6 weeks) only after security review.
Phase 3 (GA) full Console rollout and API docs; create training for Solutions/SEs and update onboarding checklists.
Fallback: feature-flag disable or automatic PET revocation if license scanner or audit anomalies observed.
updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with Legal and Security. Legal prefers default-deny for high-risk licenses; approved PET concept for low/medium risk.
2026-03-04: Engineering spike completed for mediator service; prototype can validate PET and enforce KMS decryption flows (ENG-7123).
2026-03-07: Design shipped timeline wireframes; added stern visual for high-risk license entries per Legal feedback.
2026-03-10: Security review draft comments: require pet_id rotation and hardened deny-list management; added to technical_considerations.
2026-03-12: Scoped Phase 0 alpha and toggles; Marco to own Console integration work. Created initial e2e test plan.
notes: Trade-off: allowing evals via PET speeds vetting but requires robust logging and operational guardrails. We accept a slightly higher operational cost to dramatically reduce time-to-evaluate.
If Legal marks model as high-risk after PET issuance, system should auto-revoke and surface remediation steps; build remediation flows into timeline UI.
Consider later exposing a 'partner evaluation' PET with stronger contractual controls for vetted third parties.
